_comment: Captured 2026-09-17 against mainnet CCKXBE5GKJOCE7IKL64HLYKW3IJSUPVOLC4CS77GQT5QQHDZLDYV3DFT. The live /swaps/strict-send HTTP endpoint itself was retried against multiple real, well-funded mainnet accounts (Kraken's GA5XIGA5...GGKTM with 263308 XLM + a USDC trustline, and Kraken ColdStorage GB6DQO6L...RZCOM5 with 247M XLM + a USDC trustline; also a self-swap), several asset pairs (XLM/USDC, XLM/yXLM), and a range of amount/minToReceive values - every attempt still returned `{"message":[null],"error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}`, reproducing exactly the unresolved failure the spec's own prior research already hit (confirmed NOT account- or amount-specific: omitting a required field like `route`/`amount`/`minToReceive` instead gives a normal, specific validation message, so this null-message 400 is some other, still-undiagnosed server-side fault independent of caller input). Per the brief's fallback, the path tuple order was instead resolved from two independent, genuinely-live sources and is CONFIRMED, not guessed: (1) a direct getLedgerEntries read of the contract's own Map(u32) persistent storage for indices 0-40 (see assetMap below), and (2) 15 real `strict_send` events the contract itself emitted on mainnet between ledgers 64468572-64476412 (via getEvents), including multi-hop paths where one hop's out-index provably equals the next hop's in-index (e.g. [[4,0,1042,25],[4,25,1049,38],[4,38,1152,33]] for an XLM->USDC->(idx38)->XRF route). Cross-referencing every event's plaintext from_asset/to_asset against the Map gives one, internally-consistent answer across all 15 samples: path tuple = [protocol_id, in_asset_index, pool_id, out_asset_index]. Because the live endpoint would not cooperate, this fixture's contractArgsXDR is not a freshly quoted-and-built call but the genuine InvokeHostFunction operation extracted from a real, already-successfully-executed mainnet transaction (txHash dc911e7d85610b233e29093e27fd8ee61a3604c251984656b3b703d027c11f34, ledger 64468572, a self-swap: from==to==GB35ULWRFMUSI2BAAUVKH3CJ37UIXRUCM4AIMBBPAZ76IUK3RVHEELH7, fetched via Horizon and decoded with this repo's pinned @stellar/stellar-sdk exactly per the brief's Step 2 snippet) - arguably stronger evidence than a self-built quote, since it is proof the exact bytes executed successfully on-chain, not merely that they simulated. Confidence: high (not merely plausible - two independent live data sources agree with each other and are non-guessable, since the pool ids and protocol ids are opaque integers that only make sense if the index positions are as stated).

sourceTransaction.note: A real, already-successfully-executed mainnet strict_send call, not a freshly built one - see _comment.

assetMap._comment: The contract's own Map(u32) persistent storage, read directly via getLedgerEntries against mainnet.sorobanrpc.com on 2026-09-17, indices 0-40 (an arbitrary cutoff for this fixture, not the contract's full table). Index 0 and index 37 both resolve to XLM's SAC - the admin registered the same asset at two indices, which is why one of the corroborating XLM->XRF events above uses fromAssetIndex 0.
